regla_guardable: Cloudy or not: SPF 30 or higher, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, reapply every two hours.

interaccion.guardar: SPF 30+, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, reapply every 2 hours.
interaccion.comentar: Do you wear sunscreen on cloudy days? Yes or no?

fuentes: American Academy of Dermatology (aad.org/news/survey-shows-sun-protection-lacking-in-winter): even on cloudy days, up to 80 percent of the sun's harmful UV rays can penetrate the clouds; broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen SPF 30 or higher on all skin not covered by clothing; reapply every two hours or after sweating; snow reflects the sun's damaging rays
U.S. EPA, UV and sun safety (SunWise): UV can't be seen or felt; clouds block some UV, thicker clouds more, but you can still burn on a cloudy day

frases.texto: You skip sunscreen when it's cloudy.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The American Academy of Dermatology says even on cloudy days, up to eighty percent of the sun's harmful UV rays can get through the clouds.
You can't feel UV. Heat and brightness aren't the same thing, so a gray sky feels safe when it isn't.
Same in winter: the academy says snow reflects the sun's rays too.
Heads up: clouds do block some UV, and thicker clouds block more. But the EPA says UV can still burn you on a cloudy day.
The rule to save: SPF thirty or higher, broad-spectrum, water-resistant, and reapply every two hours.
Do you wear sunscreen on cloudy days? Yes or no?
